newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Profit-taking sends Seoul stocks to lower close.
newsitem.headline: Profit-taking sends Seoul stocks to lower close.

text.p: Seoul stocks closed slightly lower on Thursday on broad profit-taking in response to the past two days of sharp rises, brokers said.
They forecast the market would remain weak for most of Friday but would rebound towards the close on the back of bullish investor sentiment.
The composite index closed down 2.03 points to 775.26. It fluctuated between 773.27 and 782.17.
"Despite today's weakness, the overall sentiment looked still bullish," said Hwang Chang-joong of LG Securities.
The past two days of rally were linked to the trade ministry's announcement on Tuesday that the nation had recorded the first monthly trade surplus in 30 months in June.
"The effect of the June trade figures will last further," said Park Sun-young of Hyundai Securities. "But the market needs more time to digest profit-taking selling."
Blue chips fluctuated as profit-taking selling alternated with buying by foreigners and some off-shore funds managed by local investment firms, brokers said.
Decliners led advancers by 414 to 354 as 51.2 million shares changed hands, down from 52.78 million traded on Wednesday.
The central bank's announcement that it would further liberalise bank interest rates had little immediate impact on the market.
The Bank of Korea said it would allow banks to set their interest rates on savings accounts from July 7. The rates are currently set at three percent per year.
September index futures contracts were up 0.40 of a point to 84.50 while the underlying KOSPI-200 index shed 0.24 to 81.39.
